infobox.value: A reliable, durable shield crafted from iron; perfect for tanking big hits.

description:

(Journal)
When the Glass Knife was caught, she had no concerns about safety. As a blacksmith, she was well armed; better than most of the hunters who tracked her down. She wielded a dagger in one hand and an Iron Shield in another. She snarled in defiance at any who condemned her for her crimes.

She was, after all, protecting humanity. Purging impurity. Ridding them all of the Amalgamated stain on their bloodlines. In her mind, she was doing the whole village a service. A worrying number of villagers agreed with her.

As the wife of an elder, her sentence was light. An act of community service, doing what was already her job. She wasn’t imprisoned. She wasn’t executed. She wasn’t publicly condemned for her crime. She laughed off over a dozen murders with a cruel, smug smile.

Although she carried an Iron Shield that weathered many attempted reprisals by Amalgamated enraged by the failure of justice, her real shield was the status she held. The wife of an elder, the blacksmith of the town, evidence incarnate that justice stopped when a victim was Amalgamated.

name: Kalphite Carapace Chest

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: This chest armour is made from parts of the kalphites. Its durable but flexible nature makes it excellent for rangers.

description:
Kalphite carapace chest is a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the chitinous carapace vestige from Iasadair - The Merchant.

(Journal)
Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim.

The shell of a Kalphite is strong and durable, a thick layer between them and the rest of the world. It keeps them safe, yes, but closed off from sensation and feeling, an emotional gulf between them and everyone else.

Fortunately, they’re insects and couldn’t care any less.

You, at least, are in possession of vocal chords and the ability to interact with others. You can also take off your armour,  should you ever need to—something not recommended in the middle of battle, no matter how much you’d like to improve your emotional bond with something.

It is worth noting, however, that there is an unexpected side effect to this armour. Dragons find you extra crunchy.

Young hunters would be gifted Leather Armour by their family as a sign of adulthood. Good-quality Leather Armour showed great pride in one's progeny. Many villagers would compete with one another to gift increasingly elaborate armour — as if doing so confirmed to all others that their child was special.

A leather shield consists of a thick piece of leather stretched across a wooden frame. Wooden shields are bulky and heavy, making them more unwieldy. In contrast, a Leather Shield’s relative lightness makes it much easier to move into position.

Leather shields were popular with the villagers of Bramblemead, since the materials were comparatively easy to gather. Young warriors often wielded them as they accompanied druids into the woods, where the druids gathered herbs for their medicines and rituals.

The Children of Shadows also enjoyed Leather Shields, which they decorated with Zamorakian symbols, hoping to intimidate anyone who saw them.

description:
The leggings of lightness are a piece of power level 1 leg armour, which can be crafted using a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming the suspiciously light tattered boots vestige, found in a chest atop the windmill in Temple Woods. Their special effect increases the player's maximum carry weight by 50 and reduces the amount of fall damage the player takes. Also removes the rune cost of the spell Windstep.

(Journal)
A cousin to the better-known Boots of Lightness, popular on the Gielinor mainland. These leggings were created by Shana, a Bramblemead villager who hated the cold. While the boots were functional, and useful, making it easier to carry things round the village, she always felt the winds chill no matter what she wore.

Her solution was simple. Since enchantment created an excess of energy, at least when she did it – she was never going to become a wizard – she laced the leggings with the lightness charm.

The effect was twofold. Firstly, she could carry things around the town as easily as if she were wearing the boots. Secondly, the enchantment kept her legs nice and warm.

Fortunately, the designs for these leggings improved over the years, removing the overheating problem that Shana had been so fond of. Although she was doubtless less fond of it after her house caught fire.

Progress demands sacrifice.

Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wear these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician.

The first of these robes was woven from silken threads created by the now extinct glimmeringwing moth, a species that used to dwell within the Moon Garou cities, evolving glittering wings that looked like the glass mosaic patterns used to decorate the streets.

When Fuzan razed the cities and destroyed those mosaics, the glimmeringwing moth species became a tragic casualty of his cruelty. Outside, in the sands, their sparkling wings were not camouflage, but beacons, drawing every predator to them.

A Moon Garou shaman must walk the deserts before they can be truly considered magi in their own right. They wander, explore and contemplate the loneliness of the sands as they do so.

Some hear voices, believing them to be ancestors, deities, spirits or just their own internal monologue trying to dull the silence.  Others find a profound calm in the silence, many choosing to live a quiet life in return.

Others, find monsters. There are many shamans who report that they did battle with the terrible demons creeping out from Dowdun Reach. Others battled kalphites, KotHaar or even dragons. One claims to have battled a creature that rose out of smoke, whimpering and wailing as it went, and it left the shaman’s mind shattered in return.

Yet, no matter how far the shamans wander, eventually they all found their way home, enlightened and enriched, and ready to serve their people.

Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician.

These robes are only given to a shaman after completing three mystic trials. The first is a trial of contemplation, where each applicant is given a complicated riddle to solve and three nights in which to do so. During that time they are allowed no forms of communication, and must rely purely on their ability to contemplate the words and arrive at a solution. The answers to the riddle are rarely set in stone: it is the interpretation that matters.

The second is a trial of compassion, and they are never warned of this one in advance. Indeed the trial may have happened before the applicant even entered into training. They could be tested at any point in their lives. It’s a simple trial: the applicant at some point finds someone in need and how they go about helping, or not helping them, is noted for the trial. This weeds out the cruel people pretending to be shamans, and encourages an attitude of compassion in potential applicants.

The final trial is the hardest of all, the trial of creativity. Here the applicants are given time to study magic, its forms, its methods and its malleability. To complete this trial, the applicant must create a new spell, enchantment or other form of magic, that has never been seen before. This trial has led to some of the most beautiful discoveries… and some of the most terrifying.

(Journal)
Would Dowdun Reach be standing without mithril? At the very least, it would be standing elsewhere. And since 'elsewhere' would put it in the path of dragons, the Withering and Saradominists at various points on Ashenfall's timeline, you would have to surmise that no, Dowdun Reach would not exist.

The Children Of Shadows were once little more than a disaffected rabble. They gathered with the purpose of plotting against Saradominists, but, in truth, most of their time was spent infighting. But even infighting demands a forum, and the Children of Shadows chose Fellhollow Mountains.

The mithril in Fellhollow Mountains (known at the time as Dowdun Mountains) was discovered by a young Zamorakian who wanted to make a raven habitat, something similar to a dovecote. She mined rock and hit a mithril seam. The shimmering metal stunned her, as it has to generations of dwarves.

She hid her discovery. We do not know why, but we can guess that greed played its part, as it is wont to do. Yet, her discovery was discovered, and the young Zamorakian was killed, left to be picked apart by her ravens. Ravens are an unsentimental bunch.

Mutiny followed, until the Zamorakian chaos subsided. The Children of Shadows now had mithril, a metal that was desired by many. And desire is such a wonderful tool for sowing discontent.

(Journal)
The warriors of Dowdun Reach were skilled in the manipulation of mithril metal. They made swords, axes, and great hammers that could crush their enemies flat. They crafted impressive suits of armour, though they favoured the more sinister-looking black armour than the mystical-looking mithril.

One Zamorakian blacksmith, a man called Bob, like so many people on Gielinor, crafted the first mithril medium helm to very little fanfare. He would wear it at every meeting, he would show it off at all the big events, all to impress the women of the keep. You can imagine how well that went.

Not very well, for clarity's sake.

The Children of Shadows were no miners, so the extraction of mithril from the mountain was a slow process. Goblins were forcibly employed at the cost of a little food.

Among the order, however, the Children of Shadows had some smiths. These smiths lived dual lives: forging deliberately dull weapons to arm the Saradominists in Bramblemead, and scratching together time for pilgrimages to the Dowdun Mountains. There, they would deliver hardy weapons and armour in the name of Zamorak.

Making mithril armour and weapons was not permitted, however. To do so would cheapen the metal, to make it seem widespread. Mithril, it was determined, would be a metal of bribery. It would only cross palms, not swords. By keeping it desirable in this way, the Children of Shadows could control its value, and that value would remain high. Only then could they lobby those who would further Zamorak's goals.

How innocent it all sounds now. Mithril is far from rare nowadays, and seams have been found beyond Dowdun Reach. Mithril is just another metal for blacksmiths to dally with. It is no longer a death sentence to make a dagger from it.

There was a time, before the Withering, when a choice was made. The Children of Shadows became paranoid about the prospect of attack and betrayal. It did not seem to matter that they were guarded by dragons who manufactured peace. Dark whispers moved them to act.

Their lord, a man by the name of Rasmodel, prepared an edict whereby a faction would form. This would be the Shadow Knights, and the knights would enforce the will of Rasmodel.

An aspiring knight needs weapons and armour, which led to Rasmodel's choice. Were the knights to wear mithril, the metal that now freely flowed from the mines of Dowdun? It was strong enough, but mithril's value was in its perceived rarity. Or were they to import a different metal, one that would be costly and awkward to source - particularly for a force that wished to remain inconspicuous?

In the end, the choice was made for Rasmodel. The dragon, Xikotal, had a gift. In one claw, he had coal, in the other iron. He wanted to help the Zamorakians, to bring them an offering that might soften their determination to isolate. In the dragon's optimism, the gift would bring the Zamorakians into the wider Fellhollow community.

Rasmodel had his steel. He could outfit his new order. With the misguided dragon's help, he had his knights. They would ensure the rest of Fellhollow would keep their distance.

(Journal)
A long-held frustration of the Zamorakian magi, the magical sect of the Children of Shadows, was that Zamorak never came to them. At no point did Zamorak ever set foot on the shores of Ashenfall. This fact is key to understanding the resentful mentality of the shadow mage: they feel a constant undercurrent of abandonment. It also explains why they believe that mystic cloth 'came from Zamorak himself'.

The story goes something like this: a Zamorakian apprentice-mage resolved to hang himself. He looked about his room but, so poor was he, he did not have the tools to perform that simple task. His chair could not bear his weight. His bedclothes ripped when he hung from them. He crumpled to the floor in misery.

In that moment, Zamorak came to him. The mage was awestruck. In Zamorak's hands was fibre that vibrated with magic. It hummed audibly - the mage felt that he could hear chanting from it. When the mage stared at it, the blue shimmered through hues of the rainbow, and then returned to blue.

"Take it, young mage," said Zamorak, and he handed the mystic fibres to the mage. "I will see you in the next life."

In a kind of prophetic panic, the apprentice carried the fibre to an archmage. He relayed how Zamorak had come to him and brought him - alone - this mystical new fibre. He was overjoyed. He wished for the Children of Shadows to have the fabric, and he asked permission to study it.

The apprentice was tried by a council of his peers and stoned to death. His crime was denying the will of Zamorak.

The fibre? The Archmage reverse-engineered its properties, and a new fabric was born.

A friendship, of sorts, grew between Rasmodel and their merchants.

Over the span of that friendship, Rasmodel learned about their affinity to the moon, and their need to remain untethered, nomadic. He did not pry at their religion, but wondered whether this offshoot shared the same god as their counterparts

It frustrated Rasmodel that he could not infiltrate the Moon Garou, as he did with all other civilisations: he had no one in the Reach with the physiology. So, he resolved to meet with Alric, something he deemed a last resort.

Alric suggested something interesting. He could not change the appearance of a human to resemble the Garou: that was beyond his capabilities. But the mystic cloth: within that fabric was an opportunity. The material was known to hum, to resonate. But, like a parrot, it could also retain resonance and repeat it. With work, the mystic cloth could surveil the Moon Garou.

Perhaps Rasmodel could infiltrate them after all.

Mystic cloth was only for use by the Archmage and his council. It was not only a sign of standing within Dowdun Reach; it was a sign that you should probably get on with your work. If you heard the hum of mystic cloth behind you, you had better not be doing something untoward.

The role of mystic cloth changed when Archmage Alric and Lord Rasmodel agreed to meet an attaché of Imaru and Xikotal. It was some cleric from Emberwood, looking to renew an annual trade agreement.

It was to be a routine meeting, and Alric thought nothing of it. He planned to look at the cleric with disdain and sign the contract provided. But to Alric's scorn, the envoy turned up in mystic cloth. A mystic cloth waistcoat, and a mystic cloth cap, jauntily worn. She was good-natured and jovial, which only made the interaction more painful for Alric.

Alric dared not look at Rasmodel, but he knew that there would be a smirk on that smug face. Alric burned the contract and blasted the envoy off the top of Dowdun Reach. The contract would have to wait.

The first set of dark mage robes were so named because the technique to craft them required cloth that had been dyed by a unique alchemical mixture. As the years passed and Guthix introduced runes, the mixture was replaced with subtle enchantments, though the appearance was kept the same for tradition’s sake.

Naturally, many practitioners of magic preferred this armour because of its darker aesthetic. Indeed, many rogue “dark wizards” would don this armour and use magic to engage in sinister undertakings, earning this armour’s moniker a more sinister meaning.

They appeared in the village in the dead of night as twisted versions of themselves—mindless creatures infused with a shadowy essence. Those who found themselves in their path had their lives ripped out of them until nought but an empty husk remained.

It took all the visiting Wild Knights to take them down. Arrow after arrow, spell after spell, the task seemed almost insurmountable until the light of the sun made the creatures vulnerable. In their death throws, it was as if some horrible chill fell across the world as if a door somewhere had been opened into somewhere it shouldn’t.

The cult fed on distrust, paranoia and greed, some very human traits. Among this number were three apprentices of the wizard’s guild, who were frustrated that they were not given the promotions they felt they deserved.

In their quest for power, the ‘Children of Shadows’ stumbled upon ancient vaults, repositories of the dragonkin’s long-forgotten secrets. Here, they discovered the remnants of a forbidden text, a relic of immense power. Driven by their arrogance, they chose to follow its instructions, unaware of the horrors they were about to unleash.

description:

What a KotHaar really is, is a tiny fragment of the creature you see. They are the core, a mote of consciousness that can be crushed down and down to a surprisingly small size. Their carapace, what we might call this body, is almost irrelevant to them, in the grand scheme of things. They feel no pain, no loss when it is taken from them, so don’t be too sad about your weird little friend giving you theirs.

Wear the skin of your friend with pride, adventurer! They would love nothing more than to know that at least part of them is joining you on your adventures.

(Journal)

Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

There is a common misconception that the KotHaar are a hive mind. Certainly many of them work as if they are one, but they are bound by a shared purpose, not a shared consciousness. This is a distinction that other races struggle with regularly, but it is easily understood when, as inevitably happens once in a while, one of the KotHaar turns away from their intended purpose and dares to wonder what else could be.

There are a few stories, hidden in the deserts, of KotHaar explorers found doing various things. They might spend days staring at a cactus, or they might dig through a mountainside to see what’s inside.

Perhaps this chest armour, that you now wear, might once have dreamed of being something other than its purpose. Now, perhaps, that dream has come true.

(Journal)
During the final years of Bramblemead corruption had run rampant. Nobles took more than their share and the priests who watched over them turned a blind eye in exchange for their own share of glittering coin. Those who did not possess noble blood, found that their lives became harder, their earnings became smaller and joy became a much more fleeting feeling than it had done before.

One woman decided to change that. She would attack trader caravans marked with goods for the castle, taking from their purses of coin. Tax collectors would also feel the sting of her arrows, surrendering their wealth to the woman clad in green. She was given the name Nightingale, because of the whistling noise her arrows made as they flew through the air, an almost musical tone that sent fear through her targets.

Villagers would then wake in the morning following an attack, to find purses of coin in flowerboxes, window shelves, or resting neatly under the fattest, laziest, cats.

It was on a cold winter night, that Nightingale and Moragrin finally met. The assassin had given up on interrogating the villagers and worked instead to lay a trap for the highwaywoman. A caravan, loaded with gold, made its way from village to castle under the cover of night, and Nightingale arrived to claim her bounty.

It was a short, but brutal battle. Arrows whistled through the air, making music like an orchestra. Daggers glinted in the moonlight, in a dance of death that would have shredded the life of any normal person. But Nightingale and Moragrin were evenly matched, until an errant magpie brought it all to an end.

Confused by the battle, the magpie had woken from its sleep in a mad panic and dived down at the fighting pair. The distraction was just enough for Moragrin’s blade to pierce the Nightingale’s heart and as she pulled her mask from her victim, Moragrin’s world shattered as she saw the moment the life left the eyes of her younger sister.

The Nightingale was the bane of the nobility, and they became obsessed with her destruction. Not just her capture, they needed her obliterated – gone from the memories of the population forever. But this was a tricky task indeed, because the wealth the Nightingale harvested, was given back to the people of Bramblemead, rather than lining her own coffers, making her a local hero.

So they hired Moragrin the hunter to track her down. Moragrin was a cruel and merciless assassin, trained in multiple weapon techniques. She delighted in little more than seeing the look in her victims eyes the moment they transition from living to dead.

For days she followed stories of Nightingale, wandering through the village, adopting multiple disguises that she might uncover Nightingale’s real name. In all that time she learned only one thing, that the villagers loved Nightingale and would never knowingly give her up.

(Journal)
Hate can be a powerful tool. It forges and it destroys with equal might. Grudges can last generations, well beyond the lifespans of those first slighted, and vengeance… vengeance can be eternal.

Ravanna knew this well. She stoked her hatred and turned it into a weapon. She wrapped it around her soul like a cage and unleashed the power of it into the very sky over the Highlands. A storm, driven by grief, rage and unfettered loathing, turned the clouds into agents of her vengeance and as they writhe, rage and hate, they build static charge that they unleash upon the garou that live below.

This ring was on her finger when Ulv died, and it became infused with that same hatred. At first it only turned its rage against the garou, but the problem with hate is that it festers and mutates into something worse. Everything is to blame for Ulv’s death. Every plant, every rock, every movement of the stars, they all led up to that moment and so the ring hates them too, and now it seeks, in its own small way, to take revenge upon the world.

(Journal)
A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour.

Dragons are not pets. They’re violent creatures, prone to random acts of aggression, driven by a rage that burns in their very soul. Still, Mayev was patient and she lured the dragon hatchling away from the corpse of its parent and out into the desert sands. Moonlight transformed the desert from gold to glittering silver, yet the ruby-red scales of the dragon seemed brighter than before.

Over the days, weeks and months to come, she kept the dragon secret. She brought it scraps of food, and kept it company on lonely days, and it came to see her not as a parent, not as a master, but as a friend. She saw him as the same. She named him Vakar – the flame-wrought song – and they would hunt together.

Over time, they knew each other’s strengths and could balance out their weaknesses. They hunted stronger prey, earning the respect of her tribe with the offcuts. Life was set to be everything they had both dreamed – until they met the KotHaar, and it all turned to ash.

As a cub, Mayev was never one to stay in one place. She ran round and round the caravans without a care in the world, always bringing the frustration and ire of her elder. “Be still!” were the words she heard first thing in the morning. “Be quiet!” the command she heard each night before bed. Yet, stillness and silence were as alien a concept to her as the magic of the druids - something far out of her reach.

One day, she left her camp in search of wild adventure, much to the chagrin of the camp guards. She risked the harsh sunlight of the dunes, clinging to shadows, exploring caves and passages revealed by the passing sandstorm of the day. Each morning her world was different, new paths appeared while familiar ones were hidden, and on this day she found a cavern deep underground.

There she found a red dragon, breathing her last breath, and the hatchling beside her breathing his first.

Dragonfire was little concern to creatures birthed in lava, and garou arrows bounced harmlessly off obsidian flesh. Yet, despite all this, it was the madness in their eyes that terrified Mayev the most: as if something else stared back at her. Something bright, radiating a heat greater than the sun and it took every ounce of willpower not to fall to her knees in worship.

Yet, she was prey now. The hunter became the hunted and the KotHaar fell on Mayev and her dragon before she could ready a defence. She fought bravely, desperately, but it would not save her and she readied herself for a death that never came.

Vakar dived into the fray, grasping her in jaws that could have severed her in two as easy as breathing. He carried her to safety. When she came to, she saw the spears, blades and shards of obisidian pressed deep into her friend and she held him in his last breaths, thanking him for her life.

She buried the heart of her friend, as was garou custom, and crafted armour and bow from his scales and bones. Her friend would be with her, always, as companion in her hunt.

name: Reinforced Body

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A heavy chestplate made from Leather and Bone.

description:
Reinforced body is a power level 2 armour piece that can be crafted at a crafting table.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force.

There was a bountiful supply of leather in Brynmoor, much to the chagrin of cows. Young villagers would craft sturdy leather armour when they trained with the guard. Few villagers would ever make the cut of town guard; the demands were strict, and the discipline required was more than many could handle. Yet, those who made the cut were afforded the utmost respect among the people.

At least those who were not afflicted by the curse of the Amalgamated.

name: Reinforced Helmet

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Protect your noggin with this basic headgear made from leather and bone.

description:
A reinforced helmet is a power level 2 armour piece that can be crafted at a crafting table.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force.

While metal is the preferred material for armour, leather has its charm. Its wearers boast greater agility and find it easier to hide the sounds of their movements than they can in metal gear. But its most important benefit is the relative cheapness of its construction.

name: Reinforced Legs

infobox.label: description

Reinforced legs are a power level 2 armour piece that can be crafted at a crafting table.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force.

When Amalgamated rose through the ranks of the guard — a tricky feat given the prejudice against them — it did not instill the populace with a sense of comfort. The villagers would see the marks of the elemental corruption on the guards and would turn and walk the other way. They would refuse to report a crime if they saw leaves instead of hair.
Amalgamated guards would rarely be granted equipment of greater quality than reinforced leather — no matter what the mission they were assigned. It was seen as a waste, considering the uncooperative nature of many villagers, making it hard for an Amalgamated guard to do their duty.

It is, perhaps, no wonder that few Amalgamated guards chose to remain in the service for long.

name: Ring of Life

infobox.label: specialeffect
infobox.value: When close to DEATH, TELEPORTS you to your current BED

description:
The ring of life is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players automatic teleportation to their bed or bed roll upon reaching 10% health. Once that happens, the ring becomes broken, requiring 2 Vault Core to repair. The recipe is unlocked through Death's Exchange for 800 soul fragments.

(Journal)
Harold has a job for you and won’t let something as trivial as your expired mortality get in the way. This piece of enchanted jewellery is primed to go off when you’re about to land on Death’s list, whisking you away to safety before the scythe needs to be swung.

There are many sorcerers that have studied these rings for years, going slowly mad as they try to uncover the secrets of immortality. If they could just learn the methods by which this ring operates, they could extend their lives indefinitely.

Only one wizard ever actually learned this secret, but he forgot the method by which this ring works, for it teleports you at the moment of your death. As the ring does not stop the aging process, this unfortunate mage now spends his eternity in perpetual teleportation – hurled through the abyss, never to take form again.

(Trivia)
* There was a bug where the ring would vanish once activated. It was meant to be in a broken state and recharged with vault cores instead.
* In both RuneScape and Old School RuneScape, the ring of life vanishes the moment it is active.

name: Ring of Recoil

infobox.label: specialeffect
infobox.value: A PERCENTAGE of DAMAGE received is DEALT back to ATTACKERS

description:
The ring of recoil is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring deals percentage of damage received back to attackers. The damage dealt is equal to 50% of the damage taken, rounded up.

(Journal)
Vengeance isn’t a dish best served cold, but one served quickly. Whilst taking years to enact the cruellest retaliation might work in the civilised world, in the wilds of Ashenfall a quick strike is far more valuable.

This ring was first created by one of the Amalgamated, worn as both deterrence and for some small satisfaction when they were targeted by vigilante mobs. It didn’t prevent the bruises, or fix the broken bones, but their assailants attacks would end much more quickly when they discovered they weren’t as untouchable as they thought.

name: Rune Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A sturdy rune helm built to withstand the chaos of close combat.

description:
Rune Helm is a power level 8 armour piece.

(Journal)
It is perhaps fitting that the first pieces of rune equipment were worn by the creator of runes themselves, Guthix. Of course, rune metal is not made of runes, and indeed has no actual connection to runes at all, but Guthix, for all his many qualities, was not the greatest of wordsmiths.

The god journeyed deep into Ashenfall, where he discovered the Wellspring and the strange metal that glistened nearby from the rocks. It has a soft blue-ish hue that was both subtle and entrancing in different ways and he became intrigued. Using techniques he had learned from the dwarves, Guthix attempted to fashion the metal into equipment, yet it resisted his every effort and refused to be anything more than a strange, glittery sort of ore.

There was magic there, in the ore. It resisted pickaxes, it repelled weaponry, it practically jeered at Guthix, telling him that it was the most interesting metal around. Yet no matter what he tried, he could not tame it.

Until he discovered luminite, and then everything changed.

name: Rune Platebody

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Thick rune plates forged into armour for the strongest of warriors.

description:
Rune Platebody is a power level 8 armour piece that can be crafted on the Armour Bench. To unlock the recipe, players need to have Rune Bar crafted.

(Journal)
It is perhaps fitting that the first pieces of rune equipment were worn by the creator of runes themselves, Guthix. Of course, rune metal is not made of runes, and indeed has no actual connection to runes at all, but Guthix, for all his many qualities, was not the greatest of wordsmiths.

Luminite, somehow, limited the metal's reaction to other metals, but only within the smelting phase. It allowed the construction of bars, which in turn allowed the construction of plates which could be fitted together to form armour.

It took several weeks, for Guthix's blacksmithing skills had long fallen to atrophy, but the god was able to fashion himself a full suit of rune metal. Just in time for the Dweller to attack.

name: Rune Platelegs

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Durable rune platelegs designed for warriors who spend more time fighting than running.

description:
Rune Platelegs are a power level 8 armour piece.

(Journal)
It is perhaps fitting that the first pieces of rune equipment were worn by the creator of runes themselves, Guthix. Of course, rune metal is not made of runes, and indeed has no actual connection to runes at all, but Guthix, for all his many qualities, was not the greatest of wordsmiths.

The Dweller was a beast that had nestled into the Wellspring and the energies had transformed it into something more than it was. What had previously been nothing but an unpleasantly large arthropod, was now a great lumbering beast full of hunger and fury. The anima had twisted it into something resembling th e colossi and it roared out of the Wellspring straight for the god of balance.

Yet, for all his desires for a peaceful existence, Guthix had the warrior's heart and he was more than a match for the Dweller. Though the battle shattered mountains and diverted rivers, the Dweller soon found itself sliced in twain by the god's terrible sword.

He cast the body into the deepest depths of the ocean, in fear that it might one day return.

name: Rune Shield

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A rune shield forged to endure punishment that would leave lesser metal in pieces.

description:
Rune shield is a power level 8 shield.

(Journal)
Nobody likes a meeting with their manager, and nowhere is that truer than in Kuldra's Tower. Kuldra would summon her troops to her chamber, and those troops would do their best to look attentive while cowering behind their shields. An onlooker might have enjoyed how the troops would poke their heads above when Kuldra's mouths were closed, and then duck behind when they were open.

Kuldra was too wise to miss this pattern. She would often treat herself, opening her mouths in sequence. She would enjoy how much her troops looked like moles, poking their heads in and out of their holes.

name: Runite Med Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A strong rune helm, for keeping important thoughts safely inside.

description:
The Runite Med Helm is a power level 8 helmet. It can be crafted at an Armour Bench using 4 Rune Bar, 4 Black Dragon Leather, 1 Vis Cloth, 1 Harmonised Compound, and 1 Draconic Vis Wax.

The recipe for this item is obtained from purchasing the Deluxe Edition.

(Journal)
The first suit of rune armour was worn by the god Guthix, after many months of failed blacksmithing attempts. For all his might, skill and wisdom, Guthix, it seemed, was remarkably poor at anything practical and that delighted him in ways he couldn't share. For Guthix had never really wanted to be a god. Though he took his responsibilities seriously, he had ascended in an act of vengeance, not by deliberate intent. In his transcendence, he had lost much of what made him happier in his mortal life. Failures, it seems, could spark as much joy as success, for one learns and grows from the experience and such growth defines who we are.

The rune medium helm is one of the first pieces he crafted. You can tell because it looks like a brick with delusions of grandeur.

name: Salve Amulet
description:
The salve amulet is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases damage against undead monsters by 17%. An effigy with a glowing ball at the Skekven Kara vault gives a stone dwarven tablet, which, after talking to Doric, grants a recipe for the salve amulet. Players will receive a salve crystal (required for creating the amulet) in return for this exchange. Loses 3 durability per hit on undead enemies, meaning it will break after ~833 hits.

(Journal)
The name is a bit of a misnomer, since this amulet has very little to do with the Salve river. Instead its name refers to the crystal that traditionally sits at the heart. This crystal was first brought to the region by Saradominist priests, sometime in the Third Age. They had harvested it from a cave near the Salve river and found ways to cultivate it on Ashenfall’s soil, by utilising the natural magic infusing everything.

Sanctified by faith and magic, this amulet was fatal to the undead, and the dragonkin Lacrussa was fascinated with the properties. She stole the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault, long before the withering curse spread over Fellhollow. Instead she had delved too deeply in her own experiments and discovered something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead.

This amulet allowed her to hold the forces back and keep them from overrunning her lab. That was until she met her end at Kuldra’s fangs.

name: Saradominist Cloak

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Worn by followers of Saradomin, this cloak reflects a commitment to justice and the light of reason.

description:
The Saradominist cloak is a reward item from completing the activity, Statues of Saradomin. Like other capes, this shares the same melee, ranged, and magic defence.

(Journal)
Priests of Saradomin would often wear cloaks like these. Simple affairs, designed to keep them safe from the breeze whilst also venerating the god of order.

Both practical and fashionable. A good Saradominist always looks their best in any weather.

description:
Shadow body is a power level 6 ranged armour that can be crafted at a armour bench.

The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the limp black lining vestige from the Evil Emporium shop.

(Journal)
The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Archmage Alric came to Lord Rasmodel with a sheet of paper. It was morning, when the Master of Dowdun was most impatient.

Alric had been monitoring the Black Knights. He had suspected something for years now, but today he had proof. The sheet was from a ledger, and it had accounted for the number of magi casualties since Alric had become Archmage. There had been one hundred and seventeen deaths from one hundred and seventeen separate incidents. There was no single incident in which more than one mage had died.

Alric was in a fury, tossing papers and spitting curses. It was proof that the Shadow Knights were deliberately negligent, that they saw the magi as disposable. Lord Rasmodel and let the mage rampage.

The orders went out from Lord Rasmodel the next day. All Shadow Knights were to allow two magi to die with each incident.

(Journal)
The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Lord Rasmodel's greatest challenge came from within. It did not carry a sword or crossbow.

The Shadow Knight numbers were dropping. It was impossible to resign from the order -- that was written in the charter -- but more and more of the knights were falling into madness. If it were physical wounds, Lord Rasmodel could have done something about the epidemic. He could amputate the problem with a single swing of his sword. But his enemy was intangible.

He decided to visit those on the precipice of madness. Most of them were unintelligible, but some talked of food not satisfying them anymore. Others called out to the Dreaming Stone like it was their mother, as if it would save them. In many cases, it sounds like the afflicted were arguing with themselves: two enemies unleashing an enmity.

One of the mindless disquieted Lord Rasmodel more than the others. She was an afflicted soldier that he knew from long ago. She rambled in a voice that mimicked the droning of a bored aristocrat. Lord Rasmodel knew that voice well. He stumbled from the bedside of the soldier and took no other visitors that day.

The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights, as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Lord Rasmodel gave his Black Knights two sets of orders. The first they were free to discuss, and were encouraged to do so. They were there to protect the magi from the demons. Should one break from its bindings, it was to be put down. In an outbreak situation, the Shadow Knights had full jurisdiction and a freedom to kill with impunity.

The second set of orders was not to be discussed, not even in the company of another. There were two salient instructions.

Instruction 1: The Shadow Knights would allow for the 'Demon's Share'. Should a demon become unruly, one single mage fatality was encouraged before the demon was to be put down. It was like the culling of rabbits. The mage numbers needed to be managed.

Instruction 2: Should the flow of demons be too much for the magi to control, the Shadow Knights were to collapse the infernal portal. This was the primary directive: the demons and magi were secondary.

name: Shadowscale Cape

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A cape worn by those from the lands of death and decay.

description:
The shadowscale cape is a stylish cape that can be created by learning the vestige from skeletal marauders and rotsworn marauders, both dropping the vestige at a 1/100 drop rate.

(Journal)
This cape is all that remains of the once proud archers of Fellhollow. Hunters and scouts who would stalk the forests and woodland hunting game to feed the other villagers. As the time dragged on their flesh and clothes have rotted away, leaving only this cape as a reminder of their existence.

name: Shadowscale Hood

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Ranger Headgear worn by the Skeleton Archer's from Fellhollow.

description:
The shadowscale hood is a power level 5 ranged armour that can be crafted at a armour bench. Players can receive the vestige from skeletal archers at a 1/100 rate in Fellhollow.

(Journal)
The last hunter in Fellhollow hid in the trees for as long as he could. Beneath him the dead shambled and stumbled and clawed at the bark, yet he remained in the trees safely out of reach.

He fed himself on nuts and berries, stealing form the treasure troves of squirrels and birds, occasionally risking a trip to the ground to hunt a passing animal. He gave up on cooking the meat he hunted, as he could not stay on the ground long enough before the dead rose up to face him, so he tore into the carcasses of deer, sheep and rats, trying his best not to vomit.

He barely noticed when his appetite changed, since he was so used raw flesh and the sickly cold taste of blood pooling in his mouth. So, when the withering began to take him, he hardly noticed.

Sometimes, if you’re quick enough, you may catch a glimpse of a skeleton in the tree branches. Even in death he fears the monsters on the ground.

name: Shroud of Noggin

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A ghostly sackcloth mask. Reduces Wither buildup while worn.

description:
The shroud of Noggin is a piece of Power level 1 head armour which can be crafted using a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming the scratchy sackcloth, found in a buried chest in Hope's Fall at the end of the unmarked activity X Marks the Spot.

Its special effect reduces the amount of Wither buildup the player takes.

(Journal)
Poor old Noggin found no peace in death, because even the gods forgot him. When he reached the River Noumenon, there was no guide to usher him through to the Afterlife. No radiant light to beckon him forward into the loving arms of those he'd lost. Instead, there was a silence and it went on and on.

Always quiet and forgettable, the universe simply failed to recall him. His name was recorded in no books of the dead. The various creatures that prey on lost souls, never once though he seemed like a pleasant meal. Instead they did nothing, except to leave him to his wandering, forgotten and alone.

Then four people went digging where they shouldn't, and that made Noggin mad. Forgettable as he was, he had always made a point of preserving the status quo and to see these four ruffians blindly digging into the sould that had never done anyone a disservice, why that was unforgivable - he couldn't let it stand. So he crept into their camp, and found the treasure they coveted, and secreted himself within the gold and silver, waiting to be found. Found he was, for when they opened the chest they saw no treasure, no jewels, no trinkets of worth - because Noggin had eaten all of them, swallowed the pieces down into the void - they found only a ghostly sackcloth head glaring back at them, with nothing but hate in its eyes.

This is that piece of sackcloth, and it's not happy to see you.

name: Skills Necklace

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Provides a small chance to get extra resources when gathering them in the world.

infobox.label: specialeffect
infobox.value: Grants a BONUS when gathering FISHING, MINING and WOODCUTTING resources in the world

description:
The skills necklace is a trinket crafted at a jeweler's bench, and has a special effect of whilst fishing, mining, or woodcutting there is a chance to double the recieved resources.

(Journal)
Not all magic is focused on the obliteration of one’s enemies; though many would argue that’s where the fun lies. No, magic can also improve the rest of one’s life in similarly impressive ways.

This necklace, favoured by artisans, miners, lumberjacks and similar, is an example of such magic. The enchantment is simple, it enhances ones luck. When swinging at a rock, you have a higher chance of finding that weak seam. If cutting down a tree, the forces acting on your cuts make it easier to fell it. You are a little luckier in your endeavours and therefore get better results.

In the Wizard’s  Tower this has caused no end of arguments. Luck, isn’t a thing. It’s not a law of creation, nor a principle on which the measured universe runs. Cause has Effect. Doing one action creates an outcome, a different action another. Luck, whilst popular with the layperson, isn’t something that can be measured or refined, it’s simply coincidence, nothing more.

Yet, this necklance proves that it must be a thing. Even though it can’t be. Therefore this little trinket has been the source of some of the longest, loudest and most violent debates for decades.

name: Spectral Chinchompa Cape
description:
The spectral chinchompa cape is a cape rewarded by Vannaka after the completion of Things That Go Boom In The Night.

(Journal)
A cloak of stitched furs taken from spectral creatures. It is uncertain how one might craft such a thing, and perhaps it would be impossible anywhere other than Fellhollow - where the world of the dead and the world of the living eerily coincide.

name: Splitbark Body

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Magical armour crafted from fine cloth and hollow bark. it has strange magical properties.

description:
Splitbark body is a power level 5 magic armour that can be crafted at a armour bench.

(Journal)
Not all druids follow the notion that one must live a life of peaceful coexistence. After all, the animal kingdom is full of conflict and conquest, predator and prey, as well as battles for dominance. Some druids feel, therefore, that to truly emulate nature one must do so fully, including tooth and claw. The problem is that druids are by nature generally on the squishier side and so they needed armour that would protect their vital areas better than their normal robes.

Soon, many druids began wearing these robes made from the bark of Ashenfall trees. The first incarnations were deeply unwieldy, taking on an ungainly and unfashionable cylindrical shape - little more than tree trunks with holes for the arms and legs. They were effective insomuch that attacks rarely got through, but they made it somewhat difficult to retaliate.

Later the wizard Lavernius realises that with a few tweaks, the addition of some elegant fine cloth, one could fashion the splitbark armour into a far more glamorous form. She took to decorating her robes with glittering gemstones and silver filigree, making her stand out from the crowd. An excellent distraction in magical duels, but a terrible spotlight for local thieves.

name: Splitbark Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Magical head armour crafted from wither-corrupted hollow bark.

description:
Splitbark Helm is a power level 5 magic armour that can be crafted at an armour bench.

Some druids feel, therefore, that to truly emulate nature one must do so fully, including tooth and claw. The problem is that druids are by nature generally on the squishier side and so they needed armour that would protect their vital areas better than their normal robes.

On Ashenfall, it was the druid Pikenmix who first tried to break out of the peace-loving mould. They learned magic that would allow them to hurl flame from their fingertips hoping it might be enough. Yet, as the enemies got too close, she soon learned that she needed a stronger defence than her meagre hood would allow.

It was when she lost in thought that she found the solution - by walking straight into a tree. Her nose broke in several places and her entire body screamed in pain, yet the tree remained unaffected by her violent interaction.

So it was that she crafted herself a helm made from the very same tree. Partially in revenge, but mostly because she knew how strong the bark could be.

After having her glittering armour stolen, Lavernius decided that she was tired of being "Miss Nice Wizard" and crafted a versino of the armour that would blend worryingly well into the local scenery. She crept up on her robbers as they spent an evening trying to prize gemstones from what remained of her helmet, and she unleashed her terrible revenge.

Thousands of chinchompas, each of them suffering from a powerful confusion, were turned upon the miscreants. The resulting explosion was so bright that it turned night into day for a moment, and the flames spread with worrying rapacity.

Later bandits soon agreed that Lavernius was to be given a very wide berth.

name: Steel Full Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A full helmet forged from Steel for Melee users.

description:
Steel full helm is a power level 5 helmet that is crafted with a armour bench.

(Journal)
It was late in the development of Fellhollow that the people needed armor. They made do with old hand-me-down leather and bronze gear, brought with them from Bramblemead, for the most part, because what need was there for armor when you were protected by dragons.

Kuldra would put a stop to that mindset in the end, but it was the Children of Shadows who forged the first steel gear in Fellhollow. One member, in particular, Sadia Vulketra, began to feel that the order lacked the strength it may one day need to defend against the Saradominist forces.

There was no war. No conflict like that in Emberwood, indeed the four major faiths got along rather well with one another. Yet, the history books told Sadia exactly what the priests of Saradomin would do to the worshippers of the god of chaos.

She forged a helmet first, with the assistance of one of her many lovers, a blacksmith Amalgamated called Vesk. The first helmet was styled with great curling horns, stained black by the forge's flames.

Naturally, this style didn't prove popular with the rest of the village, as they began crafting steel helmets of their own. They favoured a more simplistic approach and a feathered plume, to look fancy.

name: Steel Med Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A dependable helm trusted by countless adventurers.

description:
The Steel Med Helm is a power level 5 helmet. It can be crafted at an Armour Bench using 4 Steel Bar, 4 Draconic Leather, 1 Fine Cloth, 1 Sacred Oil, and 2 Vault Shard.

The recipe for this item is obtained from purchasing the Deluxe Edition.

(Journal)
With just a little bit of coal and a much better set up, you can replace your pathetic iron helmets with the much more durable steel. Steel is shinier, sturdier and just all round better for you than iron, so go ahead and hurl that iron helm off a cliff and embrace your new look in galvanised steel.

In Fellhollow the local warriors experimented with medium helms. They were lighter, easier to make and seemed like a really good idea. Oh, sure, they looked bizarre, a strange sort of cube wrapped around one's face, but there was no denying the... err... the...drip? is that what kids say these days? I lose track.

Anyway, steel, it's better than iron and no less, well, square.

name: Steel Platebody

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A strong set of well-crafted Steel platemail for Melee users.

description:
A steel platebody is a power level 5 platebody that is crafted using an armour bench. It has the exact same combat stats and durability as fallen hoplite's chest and white platebody, making them functionally identical.

(Journal)
It was late in the development of Fellhollow that the people needed armour. They made do with old hand me down leather and bronze gear, brought with them from Bramblemead, for the most part, because what need was there for armour when you were protected by dragons.

Not all members of the Children of Shadows were as paranoid as Sadia, many enjoyed a blending of faiths and would regularly attend the inter-faith meetings held by the elder priests of the different religions. Still, many felt a growing unease building, even in their idyllic village, and so they began to push for the construction of steel armour.

They took the recipes discovered by Vesk and Sadia, and they found cheaper and more efficient blacksmiths to work with. The elaborate designs favoured by Sadia and Vesk, were soon forgotten in favour of much simpler and efficient designs that could be worn by anyone, regardless of faith.

With the abundance of resources in Fellhollow, soon everyone seemed to have a set of steel armour and for many it became an excuse to forge family crests and trim with filigree that set them apart from one another.

They had no idea how necessary these suits of family armour would prove to be.

name: Steel Platelegs

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Sturdy and well-made Steel leg armour for Melee users.

description:
Steel platelegs are a power level 5 armour that can be crafted at a armour bench.

(Journal)
It was late in the development of Fellhollow that the people needed armour. They made do with old hand me down leather and bronze gear, brought with them from Bramblemead, for the most part, because what need was there for armour when you were protected by dragons.

When Kuldra arrived it was as if the air had grown heavy, pressing down on everyone. A whole village fell silent as the Godeater turned her gaze upon them. As Imaru and Xikotal rose to face her, villagers instinctively ran to don their heirloom steel armour, hoping that they wouldn‘t have to use it, but knowing in their hearts that they would.

Yet, it wasn’t Kuldra that found a use for the armour. After Xikotal’s death, Kuldra left the region, leaving Imaru to her grief. And it would be that grief and the rage that came with it that would ultimately lead to the rising dead and the sad and sorry need to fight against them.

name: Steel Shield

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A reliable, durable shield crafted from Steel, perfect for taking big hits.

description:
The steel shield  is a power level 5 shield that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

The recipe is unlocked after obtaining a steel bar for the first time.

(Journal)
There are few things as good at shielding you from harm, as a great slab of metal between you and your foe. The steel shield is more durable than its iron kin, capable of resisting greater and more deadly blows.

It was popular among Fellhollow locals, who would play a game that indicated an intelligence shortage among the population. The game consisted of one player being equipped with a crossbow and other players would hide around the area carrying steel shields. The crossbow wielder would then hunt the other players and try and fire a bolt into their shields, marking them as out of the game.

Unsurprisingly the injuries caused by this game were large and common place. Even the death of some of the players wouldn’t cause the activity to be banned. “It’s tradition”, “it’s just good fun”, “hardly anyone gets hurt”, these were the arguments made even as parents grieved the loss of their child from the game.

name: Stormtouched Cape

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A cloak depicting ancient monsters and a mage's fury.

description:
The stormtouched cape is a craftable armour piece.  The recipe is unlocked by acquiring the stormtouched cape pattern, located at the top of the Highlands Castle in the Stormtouched Highlands.

(Journal)
Centuries ago, a spell was cast over the Highlands that changed it forever. Once temperate skies became pendulous clouds filled with lightning. Electric hate that strikes at anything and everything that dares step beneath their gaze.

War changes everything, even the sky.

The land itself is strewn with the dead. Ancient skeletons of colossal wyrms, the monstrous creations of dragonkin science, lie across the terrain, dead eyes watching over everything. Lacrussa considered these monstrosities her finest work. Yet she shed no tears at their destruction. She could always make more, or so she believed.

It was a lone girl, a necromancer of great power, who turned the sky into a curse. A last act of vengeance for a fallen friend. She dug into forbidden magic, drawing power from the countless dead slain in constant conflict. The garou, lords of this region, were not prepared for the power of grief, for it was a concept alien to their primordial nature.

These stories weave into the threads of this cape, barely remembered, yet never quite forgotten.

(Journal)
Impressive! You've been touched by more than just storms!

Oh, we made that creepy. Sorry about that.

What we meant is that you've been touched by lightning, not just storms. As in, you're really rather fast. Can we try that again?

name: Studded Leather Body

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Durable armour crafted from hard leather reinforced with iron studs.

description:
Studded leather body is a power level 4 armour that can be created at an armour bench.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for its combination of agility and defence.

Dealing with the armour’s distinctive scent soon became a training tool for more dangerous hunters. It taught them to use the wind as a weapon. They would always walk against it, the wind in their faces, meaning that the garou could not smell them coming. When the weather didn’t help them, the Wild mages would cast constant subtle air spells, changing the breeze’s direction.

One Wild Mage and her friend, a strange boy who wore a wolf’s skull as a mask, got the tactic down to an art. She used strange, sinister magics to enchant bones to maintain air spells, allowing her to precisely control the wind’s direction. She used this to lead the garou into traps, where her ally would leap from the shadows, taking out the unfortunate garou warriors.

name: Studded Leather Chaps

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Durable armour crafted from hard leather reinforced with iron studs.

description:
Studded leather chaps are a power level 4 armour that can be created at an armour bench.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for its combination of agility and defence.

While the design of Studded Leather made it excellent for hunters and invaluable in battles against the garou, it fell short against those who knew its construction. Betrayal is a constant foe, and once the garou war had come to a close, the Wild Knights found themselves at the mercy of it.

Though there were more dangerous threats, with the dragons that appeared out of nowhere, there were always some that prioritised power and persecution over common sense. Daggers emerged from the shadows and drove between the plates sewn into the leather. The poison on the tips of these blades ended the life of more than a few Wild Knights.

The assassins called themselves the 'Glass Knives' in memory of the serial killer who took the lives of so many Amalgamated. To them, the strangeness of the knights was a greater threat than the dragons, and they were happy to pay the terrible price of their actions.

name: Studded Leather Cowl

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A durable helmet crafted from hard leather reinforced with iron studs.

description:
Studded leather cowl is a power level 4 helmet that can be created at an armour bench.

(Journal)
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for its combination of agility and defence.

Most Wild Knights favoured Studded Leather Armour over the more durable Metal Plate Armour. Moving through the forests required as much grace as it did guts, and stealth is always a hunter’s friend.

When they were brought into the war against the garou, the leather armour initially proved less popular. While durable and agile, leather has a strong and distinctive smell. The garou’s olfactory senses were much stronger than humans were prepared for. They were capable of tracking down the leathery smell over disturbingly long ranges. Wind magic helped to keep the scent away from them, but it wasn’t enough to eradicate it.

name: Sun Ring
description:
The sun ring is a power level 4 piece of armour, made by using three vault cores on a smithing forge. However, it is currently not in the game.

(Journal)
Glittering during the daytime, the magic of this ring makes you feel more alive in the light of the sun. It was popular among farmers who spent their lives toiling in the fields, beneath the glare of the noonday sun.

name: Tattered Cape
description:
The tattered cape is a purely decorative cape that has no defensive properties, unlike most other capes. The recipe is unlocked after crafting any piece of power level 2 armour for the first time.

(Journal)
A cape made from tattered strips of cloth.

name: TokTz-Ket-Xil

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A jagged shield of obsidian, shaped to deflect and punish in equal measure. Its edges are as dangerous as the blows it stops.

infobox.label: specialeffect
infobox.value:
Slightly increased MELEE CRIT DAMAGE
Reduced DAMAGE NEGATION

description:
The toktz-ket-xil is a power level 7 shield that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench after studying the unyielding obsidian construct vestige, a 1/20 drop from Tok-Xils. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

Its special effect increases melee damage after a parry by 15%. This only increases melee damage; it does not increase magic or ranged damage. This effect is more powerful than it seems though as all damage increases like this are multiplicative: With all of them active, damage done can easily triple. For more info, see combat.

This shield has 6 less block than most other shields at the same power level, but no damage is taken or stamina consumed with a parry. By adding this shield to all of the other damage increases, the adamant mace (for example) will deal 50 more damage every parry, with no cooldown. Compare that to the dragonblight shield at power level 7, which will do 6 poison damage per second for 15 seconds, a total of 90 damage, but only once every 20 seconds. Poison damage also does not provide Attack XP.

(Journal)
A shield of obsidian, forged and reforged countless times in the heart of the Elder Kiln. Aeons of experience defending against anything that might seek to do its bearer harm, this shield now stands as one of the sturdiest defences on the planet.

Yet, within this shield, are myriad cracks and fractures, imperceptible to the human eye, yet strained across the entire structure, down to its core. A last cry of the desperate KotHaar that wielded it, as their will was subverted by the dragon Fuzan and turned to cruelty.

If you were to gaze upon those fractures with the eyes of the KotHaar you would see a warning to all. Beware the fire, fear the sun, she whispers through the luminance from worlds of kindling ash.

name: Torch
description:
Torch is a tool item that can be wielded in the off-hand to help light up areas around the player, making it easier to see. A player can still block while wielding it, but it will only account for the blocking of the weapon in the player's main hand, and so the torch may be positioned awkwardly. Whilst wielding the torch, the durability will dwindle by 1pt/second, which will take 1800 seconds (30 minutes) before it fully degrades. When creating a new character, a torch will be spawned within the inventory.

The spell Fire Spirit largely obsoletes the use of a torch, as it frees up the offhand for a shield or allows for the use of two-handed weaponry, like bows and staves. The spell also does not use up any inventory space or encumbrance.

(Journal)
Mankind has always struggled against the darkness. The shadows hide a multitude of dangers, each of them longing to tear us apart. It is no surprise, then, that light has been weaponised. Simple wood and wrappings introduced to a flame; one then carries a small fragment of the day's protection in their hand.

Although shadows are banished by its radiance, it serves as a poor defence against steel or claw.

name: Umbral Sands Cape

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A light desert cape designed to shield against sun and sand. Offers comfort during long journeys across the dunes.

description:
Umbral Sands cape is a armour piece located in Umbral Sands. Players can find the recipe for this cape in the hills, north-east of the pyramid in the Dunes of Uzzer.

(Journal)
Reminisce on all the times that sand got literally everywhere. In your shoes. In your eyes. In your breakfast. This cape is a beautifully embroidered reminder of all the hot sun, scratchy grains, and annoying bugs trying to eat your face.

Wear it with pride.

(Journal)
Running in sand is one of the hardest things in the world, so take a bow. You've not only mastered Umbral Sands, but you've run about in it, which is something that most of us would try to avoid.

name: Whispering Cape

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A cloak that makes you shiver, even as it protects against the cold.

description:
The whispering cape is a craftable armour piece.  The recipe is unlocked by acquiring the Whispering Cape Pattern, found in a chest near the waterfall in the Whispering Swamp.

(Journal)
It is said these swamps are haunted. Those who wander it at night, tell stories of whispering that bubbles up from the fetid water.

There is a coldness to these swamps, that is more than just temperature. It reaches beneath the warmest clothing and presses itself into bone and blood. Heartbeats slow and bravery breaks beneath its touch.

The trees here are old and spiteful, their roots wrapped around the bones of adventurers, villagers, and warriors alike. They care not for goblin, human, or garou, they will strangle the remains of any within their reach.

Occasionally tiny stones will bubble from the surface, black as midnight and cold as the darkest winter night. A villager once tried to craft jewelry from these stones, thinking them beautiful. It took twelve village guard to put an end to her murder spree.

This cape is woven from the fibres of swamp plants, and shields its wearer from the swamp’s whispers. Or so the old wives tales claim.

(Journal)
A Golden Whispering Cape is a very special achievement, especially considering that you can't see where you're going half the time. I struggle to move fast anyway, but doing it in fog? Nah, you can keep your cape.

name: White Adventurer's Cape
description:
The white adventurer's cape is a simple yet stylish cape that takes no materials to craft.

(Journal)
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

name: White Desert Cape

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A White cape, stitched in an ancient desert style. Its patterns reflect a long-standing mastery of life beneath the scorching sun.

description:
The white desert cape is a stylish cape that takes no materials to craft. The recipe is unlocked after studying the white memory of Menaphos vestige, which can be found in chests in Umbral Sands.

(Journal)
A pale cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

name: White Full Helm

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A helmet worn by a member of the Holy Order of White Knights. It is pure white

description:
White full helm is a power level 5 melee armour that can be crafted at an armour bench.

The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and studying the corroded white visor vestige from the Death's Exchange shop.

(Journal)
Sir Percival Lateef was a proud man, assured of his own prowess, character and moral standing. On the mainland, he would train the other knights in swordsmanship, as well as host several long and laborious lectures on his supposed life as an explorer. He had travelled across the lands, to the frozen polar regions, and the jungles of Karamja, but no one ever seemed particularly interested in his stories.

Tired of being ignored and teased for his exploits, he took a boat and sailed it north of the mainland into regions unknown. His boat was destroyed. His crew left for dead, and he found himself on a unknown beach of strange, unnatural hues. The first human on Ashenfall for centuries, he was finally the explorer he dreamed himself to be.

name: White Platebody

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: White Platebody worn by a member of the Holy Order of White Knights.

description:
White platebody is a power level 5 melee armour that can be created at an armour bench.

The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and studying the Dented White Pauldron vestige from the Death's Exchange shop.

(Journal)
Sir Percival Lateef only had a short moment of wonder, before the horror struck. The beach he had arrived on was surrounded by cliffs, meaning his only options were to climb or to swim, and since he was wearing the heavy armour of the White Knights, he decided that sinking wasn’t an option.

It took him many hours and several near falls, but he eventually made his way up and down the cliffside, only to encounter a region filled with the ravenous undead.

As a White Knight he trained to fight such evils and he fended them off as best he could, yet there were too many for him to face alone. He was forced to retreat, to a shrine, atop a rocky island, displaying the symbol of Saradomin, and there he prayed.

name: White Platelegs

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: White Platelegs worn by a member of the Holy Order of White Knights.

description:
White platelegs is a power level 5 melee armour that can be created at an armour bench.

The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and studying the Crushed White Cuisse vestige from the Death's Exchange shop.

(Journal)
Trapped by a shrine that stood atop a rocky island, surrounded by the hungry dead, Sir Lateef prayed to Saradomin with all his strength. He begged for salvation, for a miracle that might free him, but silence was his only answer. He barricaded himself atop the monument, the dead scrabbling at his defences, their unholy growling keeping him from even a moment’s sleep. As time drew on, and hunger and thirst took him, he turned to the symbol of Saradomin in defeated rage. Where was his god? Why was he abandoned? Had he not spent his life in service of the lord of light? Enraged, he took his sword and cleaved Saradomin’s symbol from its plinth, causing it to crash to the floor. Filled with guilt, he hid the fallen piece from his sight. His last act was one of blasphemy, but perhaps an act justly performed.

name: Wild Archer Body

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Durable armour worn by a Wild Knight archer.

description:
Wild archer body is a power level 4 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench.

The recipe can be obtained from Kletterbuja Kara, a dragonkin vault.

(Journal)
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt — putting even the garou to shame.

Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. They would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day, they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

Archers of the Wild Knights were quick, silent and deadly. A joke their more melee-focused companions used to raise on those rare occasions when the knights would gather. Drink and company lead to banter and poor jokes, which created much missed laughter that the Wild Knights always enjoyed.

Archer, warrior or mage, the Wild Knights would hurl jibes at one another, without a moment’s thought. Yet, when needed, there was no stronger camaraderie and they would all die for one another.

name: Wild Archer Chaps

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: Durable leg armour worn by a Wild Knight archer.

description:
Wild archer chaps is a power level 4 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench.

The recipe can be obtained from Kletterbuja Kara, a dragonkin vault.

(Journal)

Archers worked alone, it was easier that way. They could stalk their prey, silent and slowly, sometimes taking days between kills as they followed their quarry around the lands. They would hunt monsters and people with equal focus, as dictated by the order’s commands.

To harm the wilds was to make yourself a target for the Wild Knights. To sully the green lands of Guthix, an unforgivable crime. Yet, there were always those who would risk their ire, wannabe despots and greedy fools yearning to plunder the realm.

They all met the fate they deserved, in the end.

name: Wild Archer Cowl

infobox.label: description
infobox.value: A helmet worn by a Wild Knight archer.

description:
Wild archer cowl is a power level 4 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench.

The recipe can be obtained from Kletterbuja Kara, a dragonkin vault.

(Journal)
